subject: measEq.syntax: error when attempting to constrain latent means

messages.author: 1bbbf684dcdb1170
messages.subject: measEq.syntax: error when attempting to constrain latent means
parts:
Hello all,

I am conducting a measurement invariance analysis across three groups using the measEq.syntax function and following Wu & Estabrook guidelines. I started with the configural model, then constrained thresholds, and then loadings. It appears the measure's structure, threshold, and loadings are invariant, so now I'd like to constrain means to assess if latent means differ between groups. When I use the measEq.syntax, there is no difference in my loading invariance model and my mean invariance model (exact same fit and df) and I get the following warning message:

In measEq.syntax(configural.model = EDEQ.allmodelmod3FAC, data = menEDE,  :  Latent means are not comparable across groups if their respective factor loadings and intercepts are not equal across groups.

I am able to accomplish this if I don't use measEq.syntax() and instead just use the cfa() function. That is, model fit and df are different in the means invariance model using just cfa() and not measEq.syntax(). But, I know I'm doing something wrong if it's not working with measEq.syntax() so I don't want to abandon ship and proceed in my ignorance.

Below is my model and syntax. I wanted to freely estimate all loadings and not have a referent indicator, for context. I didn't want to assume invariance of any loadings. 

#model

EDEQ.allmodelmod3FAC <- 'BodyDisL =~ NA*ede32 + ede33

OverValL =~ NA*ede29 + ede30

ResL =~ NA*ede1 + ede3 + ede4

BodyDisL ~~ OverValL + ResL

OverValL ~~ ResL

BodyDisL ~~ 1*BodyDisL

OverValL ~~ 1*OverValL

ResL ~~ 1*ResL'

#configural invariance

baseline<-measEq.syntax(configural.model=EDEQ.allmodelmod3FAC, ID.fac = "std.lv", parameterization = "theta", ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016", group = "racecat", group.equal = "configural", ordered = c("ede1", "ede3", "ede4", "ede29", "ede30", "ede32", "ede33"))

model.baseline<-as.character(baseline)

fit.baseline<-cfa(model.baseline, data=menEDE, group="racecat", ordered = c("ede1", "ede3", "ede4", "ede29", "ede30", "ede32", "ede33"))

summary(fit.baseline)

#threshold invariance

prop4<-measEq.syntax(configural.model = EDEQ.allmodelmod3FAC, data = menEDE, group="racecat", group.equal="thresholds", parameterization="delta", ID.fac="std.lv", ID.cat="Wu.Estabrook.2016", ordered=c("ede1", "ede3", "ede4", "ede29", "ede30", "ede32", "ede33"))

model.prop4<-as.character(prop4)

fit.prop4<-cfa(model.prop4, data=menEDE, group="racecat", ordered = c("ede1", "ede3", "ede4", "ede29", "ede30", "ede32", "ede33"))

summary(fit.prop4, fit.measures=T)

#loadings invariance

 EDEQ.allmodelmod3FAC, data = menEDE, group="racecat", group.equal=c("thresholds", "loadings"), parameterization="delta", ID.fac="std.lv", ID.cat="Wu.Estabrook.2016", ordered=c("ede1", "ede3", "ede4", "ede29", "ede30", "ede32", "ede33"))

model.prop7<-as.character(prop7)

fit.prop7<-cfa(model.prop7, data=menEDE, group="racecat", ordered = c("ede1", "ede3", "ede4", "ede29", "ede30", "ede32", "ede33"))

summary(fit.prop7, fit.measures=T)

#mean invariance

means<-measEq.syntax(configural.model = EDEQ.allmodelmod3FAC, data = menEDE, group="racecat", group.equal=c("thresholds", "loadings", "means"), parameterization="delta", ID.fac="std.lv", ID.cat="Wu.Estabrook.2016", ordered=c("ede1", "ede3", "ede4", "ede29", "ede30", "ede32", "ede33"))

model.means<-as.character(means)

fit.means<-cfa(model.means, data=menEDE, group="racecat", ordered = c("ede1", "ede3", "ede4", "ede29", "ede30", "ede32", "ede33"))

summary(fit.prop7, fit.measures=T)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measEq.syntax: error when attempting to constrain latent means
parts: Latent means are not comparable across groups if their respective factor loadings and intercepts are not equal across groups.

As the message says, you need to additionally constrain intercepts in order for latent means to be comparable.  If intercepts are not constrained, then latent means are simply fixed to zero for identification.  So add 1 more step (scalar invariance): group.equal=c("thresholds","loadings","intercepts").  
If scalar invariance does not significantly deteriorate fit relative to metric invariance, you can then compare scalar invariance to group.equal=c("thresholds","loadings","intercepts","means")
 
Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
